content: WikiDoc Journal Club is an online collaborative platform specifically designed for WikiDoc editors. Its primary purpose is to facilitate commentary and discussions on published medical literature. This educational initiative aims to enhance participants' reading habits, deepen their understanding of clinical epidemiology and biostatistics, and improve their ability to utilize medical literature in both WikiDoc quality improvement and clinical training practices. The sessions are structured to refine critical reviewing skills and provide a forum for editors to share and discuss academic publications. The WikiDoc Journal Club was established by the editors of the WikiDoc Foundation and the PERFUSE study group. The editorial team is composed of medical doctors with a strong academic focus. The editorial hierarchy is organized in ascending order of responsibility, starting with Deputy Editors, followed by Associate Editors, and culminating with Editor-in-Chiefs. The primary objective of this journal club is to enhance the quality of scientific research by fostering innovative approaches to interaction among WikiDoc editors. As WikiDoc operates as a nonprofit organization, it provides an ideal framework for achieving the educational goals of this platform. The specific goals of the WikiDoc Journal Club include: Conducting structured and critical appraisals of medical literature. Understanding the limitations associated with applying evidence in clinical practice. Recognizing and differentiating between weak and strong study methodologies. Gaining familiarity with fundamental statistical tests. Developing insights into specific clinical problems. Refining oral and written presentation skills. Participants will either be assigned or self-select a primary article for review, which will then be evaluated by an assigned WikiDoc member prior to the biweekly meeting. The presenting scholar bears the primary responsibility for the session. Each participant will be assigned an article, a presentation date, and a preceptor. These assignments are generally fixed and will only be altered under exceptional circumstances. Presentations should last between 15 and 20 minutes, followed by 20 to 30 minutes of discussion. The selected article must be distributed to all participants at least one week before the presentation, preferably in PDF format via email. Presenters may also choose one to three supporting articles to complement the primary article. These supporting articles may include up-to-date reviews, classic studies on the topic, or research that either supports or refutes the findings of the primary article. Presenters should describe the type of article being reviewed, such as those focused on therapy, harm, prognosis, diagnosis, symptom prevalence, or economic/decision analysis. If the article does not fall into one of these categories, presenters are encouraged to discuss the study type or seek advice beforehand. Prepared worksheets will be provided to facilitate the analysis and evaluation of the article's content. Presenters are expected to develop their presentation and produce a final critique, which should be concise, follow a review style, and reflect their personal opinion. The environment is intended to be relaxed and scientifically friendly, fostering a collaborative learning experience. The review format for the sessions includes the following components: 1. Identifying the issues addressed by the article, including the research question, its significance, its alignment with existing knowledge, and its potential to address important practice or policy problems. 2. Evaluating the appropriateness of the study design in relation to the research question and existing knowledge. 3. Assessing the study methods and determining the extent to which the findings can be attributed to these methods. 4. Analyzing the main findings to determine whether the study advances current knowledge and how it aligns with what is already known. 5. Considering the generalizability of the findings to other settings, particularly in relation to the participants' own practice and community. 6. Identifying the constituencies for the findings, including patients, and exploring how they might be engaged in interpreting or applying the results. 7. Discussing the next steps in interpreting or applying the findings and identifying new questions that arise, along with potential approaches to addressing them. Attendance and enrollment for the sessions are managed through a Google Form link titled Journal Club Meeting. Participants can enroll for each session via this link. For session enrollment inquiries, participants are advised to contact Maria Fernanda Villarreal, M.D. The Wiki Journal Club website serves as a valuable resource, offering physician-reviewed summaries of the most significant studies in medical research.
